description: Nucleoid expands live route stops into ordered itinerary legs
code:
stops = [2, 4, 6]
threshold = 3
def legs(stop) => [stop, stop + 1]
itinerary = stops.filter(stop => stop > threshold).flatMap(legs)
assert(itinerary, [4, 5, 6, 7])
threshold = 5
assert(itinerary, [6, 7])
stops.push(8)
assert(itinerary, [6, 7, 8, 9])
assert(stops, [2, 4, 6, 8])

description: Nucleoid projects live team memberships without copying related identities
code:
class Member(label):
    this.label = label
class Team(members):
    this.members = members
member1 = Member("Ada")
member2 = Member("Lin")
team1 = Team([member1, member2])
team2 = Team([member1])
members = Team.flatMap(team => team.members)
labels = members.map(member => member.label)
assert(labels, ["Ada", "Lin", "Ada"])
member1.label = "A"
assert(labels, ["A", "Lin", "A"])
team2.members = []
assert(labels, ["A", "Lin"])
team3 = Team([member2])
assert(labels, ["A", "Lin", "Lin"])

description: Nucleoid flattens nested readings once and retains scalar values
code:
packets = [[[1, 2]], [], [3, 3], "ok", false]
readings = packets.flatMap(packet => packet)
assert(readings, [[1, 2], 3, 3, "ok", false])
assert(packets[0], [[1, 2]])
assert(packets.length, 5)
assert([1, 2].flatMap(item => [item, null]), [1, null, 2, null])

description: Nucleoid freezes a fan-out definition while retaining its live rate reads
code:
values = [2, 3]
rate = 2
def fanout(value) => [value * rate]
frozen = fanout.value
live = values.flatMap(fanout)
saved = values.flatMap(frozen)
assert(live, [4, 6])
assert(saved, [4, 6])
def fanout(value) => [value + rate]
assert(live, [4, 5])
assert(saved, [4, 6])
rate = 3
assert(live, [5, 6])
assert(saved, [6, 9])

description: Nucleoid restores a fan-out relationship after a rejected callback update
code:
values = [2, 4]
def expand(value) => [value, value + 1]
expanded = values.flatMap(expand)
assert(expanded, [2, 3, 4, 5])
try:
    def expand(value):
        throw "INVALID_PROJECTION"
catch error:
    assert(error, "INVALID_PROJECTION")
assert(expanded, [2, 3, 4, 5])
values.push(6)
assert(expanded, [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
expanded.length
